modals.tour1Body: Open Protocols in the top-left anytime to browse Core, Application, and Security protocols, jump to any step, or star favorites.
modals.tour2Body: Use Simple mode for clear animations and plain-English explanations, or switch to Pro anytime for hex byte dumps, CLI terminals, and link faults.
modals.tour3Body: Click any packet to inspect its headers and layers. In Pro mode, filter frames with Wireshark expressions or export a real .pcap file.
modals.tour4Body: Switch to Simulator mode to wire routers, switches, firewalls, and servers across 20 guided labs and run real ping, traceroute, dig, and curl commands.

why.app: The actual message the programs exchange.
why.tls: Scrambles the message so only the other end can read it.
why.tcp: Adds port numbers (which program) and numbering so nothing is lost or out of order.
why.udp: Adds port numbers (which program), with no delivery guarantees.
why.icmp: Carries a network status or test message, such as ping.
why.ip: Adds IP addresses: where the packet is going across networks.
why.arp: Asks which hardware address owns an IP address on this network.
why.eth: Adds hardware (MAC) addresses for the next hop on this link.

pcap.title: Capture viewer

pcap.hostsShown: The diagram shows the {{count}} busiest hosts; the table lists every packet.
pcap.errorLinkType: This capture uses link type {{type}}, which is not supported yet.

error.too_small: That file is too small to be a capture.
error.not_pcap: This does not look like a .pcap file.
error.pcapng: This is a pcapng file. In Wireshark use File > Save As and choose "Wireshark/tcpdump - pcap", then open it again.
error.read: The file could not be read.

landing.badge: Free · Runs in your browser · No sign-up
landing.title: See how internet data actually travels — step by step
landing.subtitle: NetPulse turns networking into something you can watch. Play real protocol exchanges, inspect every packet, then build and break your own networks in a Packet Tracer–style simulator.
landing.featuresTitle: Everything you need to learn networking by doing
landing.f1b: Watch DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP exchanges move hop by hop, with plain-English notes at every step.
landing.f2b: Click any packet to see its headers, flags and raw hex. Hover a field to light up its bytes.
landing.f3b: Drag routers, switches, PCs and servers onto a canvas, cable them up and send test packets.
landing.f4b: Configure routers with IOS-style commands, VLANs, NAT, ACLs, static routes and DHCP, and watch it take effect.
landing.f5b: From a home network to BGP failover, each lab has goals, hints and a solution you can replay.
landing.f6b: Test yourself, fix broken networks in Break-it challenges and keep a daily learning streak.
landing.f7b: Open captures from Wireshark or tcpdump right in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
landing.f8b: English, Español, العربية, हिन्दी, മലയാളം and தமிழ் with right-to-left support. Install it and use it offline.
landing.s1b: Choose a starter above or open the full library.
landing.s2b: Watch packets move between devices and read the notes.
landing.s3b: Inspect headers, ports and real-world security tips.
landing.s4b: Wire up routers, switches and firewalls in guided labs.
landing.simTitle: A simulator that behaves like the real thing
landing.simBody: Configure devices from the command line, change an address or shut a port, and see the traffic react immediately.
landing.sim1: IOS-style modes, ? help and tab completion
landing.sim2: VLANs, static routes, RIP/OSPF, NAT and ACLs
landing.sim3: DHCP with relay, plus a PC desktop and command prompt
landing.sim4: Send test packets and follow every event hop by hop
landing.protocolsSub: Core, application and security protocols, each with a live scenario, quiz and notes. Click one to start.
landing.ctaTitle: Ready to watch the internet work?
landing.ctaBody: Open NetPulse and start with a protocol you already use every day.
